### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-package`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8fce225d133740c210c93bb902cc33c722770f43` — the merge of head `85fc3e5f1a84d0631a8cbdbfe28b0f777abe3b40` into base `c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8fce225d133740c210c93bb902cc33c722770f43 && git checkout 8fce225d133740c210c93bb902cc33c722770f43
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138 85fc3e5f1a84d0631a8cbdbfe28b0f777abe3b40 && git checkout -B drift-repro c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138 && git merge --no-ff 85fc3e5f1a84d0631a8cbdbfe28b0f777abe3b40

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Request: review · area A5 · head 85fc3e5f1a84d0631a8cbdbfe28b0f777abe3b40

Fixes #33535. The `sys_packages` boot hydration now carries the stored `created_at`/`updated_at` into the registry record's `installedAt`/`updatedAt` instead of the boot time; a fresh install still stamps now; an unreadable stored stamp keeps today's behaviour (no migration). Reproduced on main 4bba8b8f02 (2 red), ablation 2 red. Clause-② no, Metadata-protocol none. +230/-1, service-package only. CI was in progress at request time. os-dev report: 6888033827.

Posted 2026-11-15T02:37Z.

## Review: PASS

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A5 · Fixes #33535 (p2) · head `85fc3e5f1a84d0631a8cbdbfe28b0f777abe3b40` · Clause-② no. CI on this head: 51 check runs, 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress.

**What was checked**

- Diff read in full (5 files, +230/-1, all in `@objectstack/service-package` plus its changeset).
- The record really is the served one. `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) builds `pkg`, does `collection.set(manifest.id, pkg)` and returns that same `pkg`. `getPackage` returns `this.metadata.get('package')?.get(id)` with no copy. The HTTP door's `toPackageResponse` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`) projects that object field by field through `INSTALLED_PACKAGE_RESPONSE_FIELDS`, which includes `installedAt` / `updatedAt`. So the in-place write in `carryStoredLifecycleStamps` is what `GET /api/v1/packages/:id` serves. The test reads `registry.getPackage(ID)`, which is the same object.
- Nothing overwrites it later in the boot. The only non-test callers of `installPackage`, `enablePackage`, `disablePackage` and `updatePackageManifest` are the live install, PATCH and enable/disable doors (metadata-protocol and runtime `packages.ts`) and `engine-registration.ts` for code packages. The hydration skips an id the registry already holds. A live reinstall, upgrade, enable/disable or PATCH stamps `now`, which is correct for a live act.
- Parsing. `created_at` / `updated_at` are `TEXT` on SQLite and PostgreSQL and `VARCHAR(32)` on MySQL. Every current write binds `packageRowStamp` / `packageWriteStamp` UTC text, and `list()` passes the column through untouched. So a `Date` or an epoch number cannot reach the parser from these columns, and refusing non-strings is right. I ran the regex and `Date` construction from the diff in plain Node (not the repo's tests): `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` gives `.000Z`, `.mmm` and `.m` are kept, and `T` / trailing `Z` are accepted. Appending `Z` matches the UTC the writers use. Legacy SQLite `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` and MySQL `UTC_TIMESTAMP()` text read correctly. Garbage, `''`, `null` and numbers give `undefined`, so the record keeps the registry's own stamp. Out-of-range fields such as `2026-02-30` roll over in V8 rather than being refused, but no writer produces them.
- Tests. `installed-at-after-restart.test.ts` runs the real stack (ObjectQL, better-sqlite3 on a file, this plugin, the protocol) and boots a second kernel on the same file. It covers two restarts, an upgrade (the version's `created_at` is truncated to the second and `updated_at` keeps its milliseconds), and a fresh install after a restart. The `packageStampToIso` unit test covers both stored forms and the refusals. I did not re-run the ablation. Removing the carry call leaves the registry's `now` (the faked 11:00) on the record, so the two restart cases would go red as reported.

**Semver**

`patch` is right. Metadata-protocol is `none`: no spec, schema or wire-shape change. Clause-② `no` is right: `packageStampToIso` lives in `package-table.ts`, which `index.ts` does not re-export, and the package exposes only `"."`. Its root exports (`PackageServicePlugin`, the existing interfaces and constants) are unchanged.

**Nits (none blocking)**

- N1: A version change made through PATCH still drifts after a restart. `PATCH /packages/:id` with `version` keeps `installedAt` live (`updatePackageManifest`). It then persists through `publish`, which inserts a new `(id, version)` row with `created_at` set to the PATCH time, and `list()` hydrates from that row. After a restart `installedAt` therefore reads the PATCH time, which is the PATCH contract the issue cites. The store cannot tell this apart from an upgrade, so this seam cannot fix it. Please add it to the acceptance notes or changeset next to the overwrite and enable/disable cases.
- N2: The pre-#31530 PostgreSQL stamp form is not read. The `package-table.ts` header records that form as fractional seconds with a `+00` offset (for example `2026-11-08 14:40:07.912345+00`), and `packageStampToIso` returns `undefined` for it. On such a row that was later overwritten, `created_at` stays in the old form while `updated_at` is in the new one. After a restart the record then shows `installedAt` = boot time and `updatedAt` = the stored time, which is earlier than `installedAt`. Accepting `\.\d{1,6}` plus an optional `[+-]HH(:MM)?` offset would cover it. Otherwise, leave `updatedAt` unchanged whenever `installedAt` could not be carried.
- N3: The new test file depends on test order. `nextPackageWriteInstant` keeps `lastPackageWriteMs` at module level for the whole file. Case 1 only gets `updatedAt` = `10:00:00.000` because it runs first. If it ran after case 2 (for example under `sequence.shuffle`), its write would be moved past case 2's `10:30:00.250` and the assertion would fail. Distinct clock times per case would remove the dependency.

Nits only, so this is the final round.
